summary: Applying an uncursed ordinary bell reaches apply.c:doapply(BELL), but JavaScript refuses that object arm before use_bell. C rings the bell and wakes nearby monsters. The selected path has no bell-branch RNG; the whole use_bell function also covers cursed ordinary bells and charged Bell of Opening state.

source.branch: For an uncursed ordinary BELL with the hero neither underwater nor swallowed, use_bell calls Hero_playnotes, prints the ring message, enters the ordinary branch without the cursed nymph roll, sets wakem, then calls wake_nearby(TRUE). Other branches cover muffling, discharged or charged Bell of Opening, invocation location, cursed nymph summon or undead creation, object charge, opening and finding, and discovery updates.
callers: cmd.c command a dispatches to apply.c:doapply, whose BELL and BELL_OF_OPENING arms call use_bell(&obj); js/cmd.js dispatches to js/apply.js:doapply, whose named-arm refusal currently includes both types.
dependencies: invocation_pos and On_stairs are consumed in the invoking predicate even for an ordinary bell; preserve evaluation order and avoid adding RNG.
obj_to_instr supplies Hero_playnotes; Hero_playnotes and wake_nearby are void side effects, while use_bell can null the object pointer after shattering.

The cursed ordinary branch consumes mkclass, makemon, obj_resists, and rn2/rnd results; the charged Bell of Opening branches consume openit/findit results and update charges, age, knowledge, punishment, and nearby-monster state.
The selected ordinary-bell path must execute wake_nearby(TRUE) through a real source-backed caller, not merely print the ring message.

evidence: At evaluation commit 35deeae3b45298577e919836bfad5c2da681ab6b, challenges/evaluations/20260929141337-v13.json reports synthetic/v13/ordinary-bell-rings 26/27 matching screens and cursors and first stop at zero-based step 26, an unported doapply object-type-255 arm. The immutable C recording is challenges/cases/v13/ordinary-bell-rings.session.json, SHA256 04413b86de4003f2eabfc16c50d4c1d570d2df29538a72d06395da6a753c1a0d.

The C recording segment 0 step 26 follows input n and displays “You ring the bell.” with no use_bell random draw. The independent recipe wishes an explicitly uncursed ordinary bell and applies its C-observed inventory letter; the recorded screen confirms that the use_bell ordinary path is reached.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:1202-1321 defines the complete use_bell branch tree. Lines 1211-1212 call Hero_playnotes and ring-message output; lines 1223-1250 distinguish cursed from uncursed ordinary behavior and set wakem; lines 1314-1315 call wake_nearby(TRUE). Lines 4333-4335 wire both bell types in doapply.

JavaScript js/apply.js has BELL and BELL_OF_OPENING in DOAPPLY_UNPORTED_NAMED_ARMS and no use_bell implementation. The source function and caller must be ported together, with consumed-return dependencies and independent evidence for active branches.
